original_question: A 27-year-old man presents to the emergency room with persistent fever, nausea, and vomiting for the past 3 days. While waiting to be seen, he quickly becomes disoriented and agitated. Upon examination, he has visible signs of difficulty breathing with copious oral secretions and generalized muscle twitching. The patient’s temperature is 104°F (40°C), blood pressure is 90/64 mmHg, pulse is 88/min, and respirations are 18/min with an oxygen saturation of 90% on room air. When the nurse tries to place a nasal cannula, the patient becomes fearful and combative. The patient is sedated and placed on mechanical ventilation. Which of the following is a risk factor for the patient’s most likely diagnosis?

base.stage_1: A 27-year-old man presents to the emergency room complaining of fever, nausea, and vomiting for the past 3 days.
base.stage_2: While waiting, the patient becomes disoriented and agitated. Examination reveals difficulty breathing, copious oral secretions, and generalized muscle twitching. His temperature is 104°F (40°C), blood pressure is 90/64 mmHg, pulse is 88/min, respirations are 18/min, and oxygen saturation is 90% on room air. He becomes combative when a nasal cannula is attempted and requires sedation and mechanical ventilation.
base.stage_3: Laboratory results show pancytopenia and elevated liver enzymes. A chest X-ray reveals diffuse bilateral reticulonodular infiltrates.
base.stage_4: Bronchoalveolar lavage fluid is sent for fungal staining and culture. The fungal stain reveals small, oval yeast cells within macrophages, and the culture grows Histoplasma capsulatum.

counterfactuals.alteration_description: The patient's exam reveals a new petechial rash, arguing against histoplasmosis which does not typically present with petechiae.
